label: toii~toii
title_raw: 〜といい〜といい [〜といい〜といい] (toii~toii)
title: 〜といい〜といい
meaning: In terms of both ~ and ~; in terms of ~ as well as ~; from the perspective of both ~ and ~
meaning_example: From the perspective of the colour as well as the design, this suit is a good match for you

notes.text: Ref # Kanzen Master Level 1 - p49 - no.49
Ref # A Dictionary of Advanced Japanese Grammar p628
notes.html: Ref # A Dictionary of Advanced Japanese Grammar p628

notes.text: This grammatical structure is used to present multiple perspectives when describing a person or a thing. It is often used to provide the speaker's / writer's judgment of the person or thing.
notes.html: This grammatical structure is used to present multiple perspectives when describing a person or a thing. It is often used to provide the speaker's / writer's judgment of the person or thing.

examples.japanese: このスーツ、色といいデザインといい、お客様はよく似合いですよ
examples.body_text:
このスーツ、色といいデザインといい、お客様はよく似合いですよ 

		From the perspective of the colour as well as the design, this suit is a good match for you
examples.body_html:
このスーツ、色といいデザインといい、お客様はよく似合いですよ  
From the perspective of the colour as well as the design, this suit is a good match for you

examples.japanese: 内容といい話し方といい、見事なスピーチでした。
examples.body_text:
内容といい話し方といい、見事なスピーチでした。 

		It was a splendid speech in terms of content as well as delivery.
examples.body_html:
内容といい話し方といい、見事なスピーチでした。  
It was a splendid speech in terms of content as well as delivery.

examples.japanese: 家柄といい学歴といい、彼は非の打ちどころがない。
examples.body_text:
家柄といい学歴といい、彼は非の打ちどころがない。 

		He is just perfect, both in terms of his family and educational background.
examples.body_html:
家柄といい学歴といい、彼は非の打ちどころがない。  
He is just perfect, both in terms of his family and educational background.

examples.japanese: スピードといいパワーといい、今の彼に勝てる選手はいない。
examples.body_text:
スピードといいパワーといい、今の彼に勝てる選手はいない。 

		No player can beat him now in terms of either speed or power.
examples.body_html:
スピードといいパワーといい、今の彼に勝てる選手はいない。  
No player can beat him now in terms of either speed or power.

comments.text: Could it be that  いい  is the stem of the verb 言う? Or perhaps the expression originated from that?
comments.html: Could it be that  いい  is the stem of the verb 言う? Or perhaps the expression originated from that?
